(4)  The Commissioner-General or any other tax official
may make copies of books of account or other documents
that are produced for purposes of this section, or may retain
them  where  such  course  of  action  appears  to  the
Commissioner-General to be necessary for the purposes of
any prosecution or the substantiation of any assessment.
(5)    Subject  to  subsection  (8)  of  section  122  and  this
section shall have effect notwithstanding anything contrary
in any written law relating to confidentiality, privilege, or
the public interest with respect to the production of or access
to documents or other evidence, including a law relating to
bank secrecy and any contractual duty of confidentiality.
